objective: To improve general written English as well as to identify and eradicate bad writing habits in areas of particular difficulty (e.g. refined use of verb tenses, more complex sentence structures, appropriate style and register).; To develop more effective writing and presentation skills for academic essays for publication (style & register, sentence structure/complexity, presentation of research); To develop general competence in the appropriate format for academic publications
prerequisites: Students should have a minimum course entry level equivalent to CER C1/C2
title: English - Writing Academic Research Papers C2

name: English - Advanced Business Communication C2
content: Authentic texts and case studies from the fields of business and economics form the basis of the course and exercises. Topics covered include: Energy; Employment Trends; Business Ethics; Finance and Banking; World Markets; Product Innovation; Mergers and Acquisitions; Debt Management; Strategy; E-commerce; Project Management; Management Accounting. Reading, Writing, Listening and Speaking skills will be practiced in classroom activities relating to these topics. Grammar and vocabulary building form part of the core of each topic module.
objective: Students will: expand general and specialized business vocabulary with focus on economic issues; enhance general communicative and grammatical competence; deepen their understanding of key economic issues and acquire the language appropriate to discussing them in English; develop and practice their business presentation skills
prerequisites: This is a C2 level course and you need to complete the placement test before the first lesson (bring a printout if your result!).
title: English - Advanced Business Communication C2

name: English - Great Minds in Science and Technology C1
content: Trust in science has been diminishing over the last 20 years or so, in part due to debates surrounding climate change. In this module, questions regarding what science can and cannot do will be discussed, as well as more basic questions like what is science? why is science sometimes under attack? should it be trusted (and why or why not)? and how does science progress? The discussion of these topics will be guided by reading texts by well-known philosophers of science including Thomas Kuhn, Richard Feynman, Jim Al-Khalili – and Naomi Oreskes, among others.
objective: Upon completion of the course, the student will have improved speaking, reading and writing skills and expanded her/his vocabulary with regard to science.
prerequisites: B2 or C1 English and an interest in science
title: English - Great Minds in Science and Technology C1: Philosophy of Science Module

name: English - English for Computer Science and the Tech Industry C1
content:
Level up your technical English and communicate complex ideas with precision, authority, and impact.

Designed specifically for advanced English speakers in CS and technology, this C1 course bridges the gap between deep technical expertise and high-level professional communication. Whether discussing Machine Learning, AI, Robotics, Data Science or any other contemporary issue in tech, this course gives you the precise vocabulary and fluency you need to excel in the industry.

Who Is This Course For?
This course is ideal for advanced (C1) English learners pursuing careers in software engineering, data science, cybersecurity, cloud architecture, or tech research who want to speak, write, and present with total confidence in international settings.
objective:
- Master Technical Terminology: Fluently use precise, advanced vocabulary across core tech domains, including AI, Machine Learning, Cybersecurity, Cloud Computing, and Computer Architecture, in professional and academic settings.  

- Articulate Complex Technical Concepts: Clearly explain issues such as low-level programming mechanics, simulation models, and performance optimization techniques to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.  

- Engage in High-Level Discussion and Debate: Lead and contribute to nuanced conversations on emerging tech trends like data science strategy, ethical AI deployment, and cybersecurity threat mitigation.  

- Deliver Impactful Tech Presentations: Structurally present topics such as software designs, system architecture, and research findings with professional confidence, clarity, and authority.

Enhance Professional Technical Communication: 
- Write about tech issues using natural C1-level phrasing.
prerequisites: None
title: English - English for Computer Science and the Tech Industry C1

name: English - English for Nerds: Learning with Sci-fi and Fantasy C1
English - English Grammar Advanced C1
content: The course gives students a thorough knowledge and practice of grammatical topics at the C1 level. Importance is placed on communicating using advanced structures and on developing a strong knowledge of the rules and nuances involved.
objective: Students will develop their knowledge of and become confident in using advanced English grammatical structures.
prerequisites: Students should have at least a B2 level of English before attending the course.
title: English - English Grammar Advanced C1

name: English - Poetry and Design C1
content:
As TUM students, many of you are engaged in design on a daily basis, whether writing program code, rethinking how traffic moves through a city (or a package around the world), designing new lab set-ups, or constructing an engine. This course introduces you to poets who do something similar with language -- and shows how their work can enhance yours. 

Over three months, we will read and analyze 12-20 poems in English, spanning more than four centuries, and look at how each might deepen or expand our understanding of design principles from fields across the TUM academic landscape. Our weekly 90-minute sessions will involve short presentations in which the poems' form, historical context, and interpretations are introduced, as well as group discussion, writing exercises, guest lectures, and recitations.
objective: Students will leave the course understanding a range of poetic devices, as well as how they might be applied to their own fields of study. Students' English vocabulary, writing, presentation skills, and agility in conversation will also develop through their participation in the course.
prerequisites: Students need not have any experience with poetry.
title: English - Poetry and Design C1

name: English - Professional English for Business and Technology C1
English - Management and Shakespeare C1
content: This course will build on four Shakespeare plays (Macbeth, Richard II, Henry IV, and King Lear) to help students recognize and analyze various principles of management, become more sensitive to interpersonal issues, and understand language and concepts that have shaped the contemporary Anglo-Saxon world. It will focus on aspects of leadership vs management, the value of money, risk, conflict management, personal/cultural identity and, last but not least, the art of successful communication: "The power of the word to change the world."
objective: After completion of this course students can understand a wide range of demanding, longer texts, and recognize implicit meaning; they can express themselves fluently and spontaneously without much obvious searching for expressions; they can use language flexibly and effectively for social, academic, and professional purposes; and they can produce clear, well-structured, detailed texts on complex subjects, showing controlled use of organizational patterns, connectors, and cohesive devices.
prerequisites: Ability to begin work at the C1 level as evidenced by your score on the placement test at www.moodle.tum.de. (Please check current announcements as the exact percentages may vary each semester.)
title: English - Management and Shakespeare C1

name: English - English for Technical Purposes C1
content: In this course, selected verb forms and grammatical structures will be reviewed and practiced, as necessary and tailored to the class's needs. These may include: gerunds and infinitives, reported speech, passives, modal verbs, present perfect and past simple, as well as all types of conditionals. Oral and written communication skills needed in professional life will be introduced and practiced, as well as aspects of intercultural communication needed for achieving professional success. Emphasis is placed on developing strategies for continued learning.
objective:
After completion of this module, students can understand the main ideas and details of not only complex texts on both concrete and abstract topics, but also technical discussions in their fields of specialization; they can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction with native speakers quite possible without strain for either party; they can produce clear, detailed texts on a wide range of subjects and explain clear viewpoints on a topical issues.

Corresponds to C1 of the CER.
prerequisites: Ability to begin work at the C1 level of the GER as evidenced score in the range of 60-80 percent on the placement test at www.moodle.tum.de. (Please check current announcements as the exact percentages may vary each semester.)
title: English - English for Technical Purposes C1

name: English - Intercultural Communication C1
content: This course, taught in English, should familiarize you with the principal theories of intercultural communication as well as providing a practical toolkit for approaching intercultural encounters through examination of critical incidents. You will also improve your ability to communicate effectively in a global context. We will view film clips, do simulations and hold discussions. Course enrolment is limited to 20 participants.
objective: After completion of this course, students can communicate more effectively with partners from other cultures. Specifically, they can recognize cultural differences when they occur, understand some specific ways in which cultures can differ, and have developed self-awareness of their own cultural behaviors and values, which helps them be more effective in cross-cultural communication situations. After completion of this course, non-native speakers of English can better understand a wide range of demanding, longer texts, and recognize implicit meaning; they can express themselves fluently and spontaneously without much obvious searching for expressions; they can use language flexibly and effectively for social, academic and professional purposes and they can produce clear, well-structured, detailed text on complex subjects, showing controlled use of organizational patterns, connectors and cohesive devices; They are better prepared for studying or working abroad. Corresponds to C1 of the CER.
prerequisites: Ability to begin work at the C1 level of the GER as evidenced by your score on the placement test at www.moodle.tum.de (Please check current announcements as the exact percentages may vary each semester.)
title: English - Intercultural Communication C1

name: English - English Through Cinema C1
content:
Our focus this semester is: Sustainable Worlds and Dystopian Futures.

Sessions will include film screenings and in-depth discussion of various aspects of culture and communication. During the course of the semester, you'll be able to find a list at moodle showing which films will be viewed in each session.

The films viewed this semester will all focus on the portrayal of science and technology in popular films, even venturing into the realm of speculative fiction.
objective:
a. To provide students with an inside view of the English-speaking world through viewing of films.
b. To develop students’ spoken and written accuracy and range of vocabulary around specified topic areas.
c. To develop fluency in interactive communication in English through guided and freer discussion of issues related to topic areas.
d. To provide critical feedback on presentations and allow students to hone the skills and language needed to deliver information and opinion effectively. 
e. To develop students’ critical faculties and intercultural ‘literacy’; to familiarize students with some key critical concepts in cultural studies.
title: English - English through Cinema C1

name: English - Focus on the USA C1
content:
This course helps students prepare for studying or working in the (post-election, Trump-era) United States, and increases their awareness of cultural differences they can expect to encounter in their dealings with US Americans. Common stereotypes about U.S. Americans as being superficial, or having ‘cowboy’ mentality, will be examined. Soft skills are learned and practiced in the English language.

Course participants will discuss life in the United States of America focusing on several prominent threads which permeate American society and which underlie some of the major differences which set American culture apart, such as Americans’ attitudes toward freedom, the pursuit of happiness, patriotism, nature, religion, and cultural diversity. By looking at textual and documentary evidence (such as life stories, radio, TV and current cinema) we will examine some of the systematic ways in which individuals enact and transform local and national identities, considering the role of institutions (e.g. church, state, commerce, family), language, habits, myths, and ideals in the distribution of power.
objective: After finishing this course you will be familiar with the basic core values which have shaped American institutions and be able to use them in analysing artifacts of U.S. culture.
prerequisites: Ability to begin work at the C1 level of the GER as evidenced by a score in the range of 60 – 80 percent on the placement test at www.moodle.tum.de. For students who test in the 80 - 100 point range, the course can be completed for credit at the C2 level.
title: English - Focus on the USA C1

name: English - English Writing for Social Scientists C2
content:
This course is aimed at students currently writing in the social sciences (seminar papers, vignettes, theses). The sessions aim to introduce students to academic writing techniques with examples from the social sciences, introducing stylistic guidelines for forceful and clear English writing at a high academic level. Students will be expected to regularly provide examples of their own writing on which they receive targeted feedback from both the peers and instructor.

Although students from all departments are welcome, this course is designed specifically for students in the RESET and STS programs. Students from political science or education are also encouraged to join.
objective: After completing this course, students will be able to express themselves with greater clarity and precision in written English. They will become more familiar with strategies for effective academic writing in English specifically, while gaining a sense for potential contrasts with their own native languages. Students will develop techniques to implement compelling sentence constructions, create cohesion within and between sentences, and render paragraphs coherent through specific semantic and syntactic choices.
prerequisites: Ability to begin work at the upper C1 or C2 level of the GER. Basic understanding of grammatical terms (e.g., parts of speech, subject, verb, object, active, passive, nominalization).
title: English - English Writing for Social Scientists C2

name: English - Introduction to Academic Writing C1
content: This course will help students learn to express themselves more correctly and persuasively in written English. There will be a focus on forming correct sentences and paragraphs, working towards the production of longer texts of the type students will be expected to write during their academic studies. They will also learn to evaluate and interpret the written texts of others.
objective: After completion of this course students will be able to write academic texts with greater fluency and accuracy and with fewer grammatical errors. They will be able to engage the rules of composition to construct logical and mature descriptions, explanations, and claims of the sort they will need throughout their academic years and beyond.
prerequisites: This is a C1 level course and you need to complete the placement test before the first lesson (bring a printout of your result!).
title: English - Introduction to Academic Writing C1

name: English - Academic Writing C2
content: The class will consist of in-class peer group sessions as well as written essays which will be subject to a series of revision. The students will be expected to critically evaluate model essays as well as their own writing in order to produce a polished finished product, which will reflect the kinds of academic writing they will be expected to do during their studies.
objective: After completion of this course, students will be able to write demanding formal texts with a high level of fluency and accuracy. They will also learn to evaluate and interpret the written texts of others.
prerequisites: This is a C2 level course and you need to complete the placement test before the first lesson (bring a printout if your result!).
title: English - Academic Writing C2

name: English - English for Scientific Purposes C1
content: In this course, each week articles to be read and videos to be watched are assigned.  In the following week, there are active small group discussions about the articles and videos assigned.  In addition, each week some elements of English grammar are reviewed.  Finally, there are also written assignments that must be completed.
objective: On completion of this course students will have expanded their knowledge of vocabulary related to science. The students reading, writing and listening skills as well as oral fluency will have improved.
prerequisites: Upper B2 or C1 level according to the online placement test at www.moodle.tum.de.
title: English for Scientific Purposes C1

name: English - English in Science and Technology C1
content: This course enables students to practise scientific and technical English through active group discussions and delivery of subject-related presentations.
objective: On completion of this course students will have expanded their knowledge of vocabulary related to science and technology. The students' reading, writing and listening skills as well as oral fluency should improve.
prerequisites: C1 level according to the online placement test
title: English in Science and Technology C1

name: English - Transatlantic Relations: Current Affairs in the U.S. and the E.U. C1
content: In this course grammatical forms are reviewed and practiced with a focus on topics of interest to students preparing for professions in business and technology branches. The course includes opportunities for students to practice both written and oral communication needed in professional life, with emphasis on career skills such as questioning techniques, negotiating, prioritizing, problem solving, and persuading, as well as aspects of intercultural communication needed for achieving professional success. Emphasis is placed on developing strategies for continued learning.
objective: and spontaneously without much obvious searching for expressions; they can use language flexibly and effectively for social, academic and professional purposes and they can produce clear, well-structured, detailed text on complex subjects, showing controlled use of organizational patterns, connectors and cohesive devices.
prerequisites: Ability to begin work at the C1 level as evidenced by your score on the placement test at www.moodle.tum.de. (Please check current announcements as the exact percentages may vary each semester.)
title: English - Transatlantic Relations: Current Affairs in the U.S. and the E.U. C1

name: English - The Science of Science Fiction C1
content:
Can members of a society without a tradition of science fiction make revolutionary scientific discoveries and produce game-changing technological developments? It is, of course, a provocative question. However, one issue I would like us to consider in this seminar is the relationship between thinking outside the box and being able to bring that thought to bear on the physical world and also be aware of the ethical consequences of our actions.

Starting with Jules Verne, and even Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein, authors have used the medium of fiction as a vehicle to speculate on the possibilities of science and technology and to imagine its potential for helping human beings as well as harming them. This ability to think beyond current knowledge and capability and to consider its implications for human life is certainly as important today as ever, on one hand as fuel to propel further growth and on the other hand to help to steer and guide it. 

In this colloquium-style seminar, we will select various works of popular science fiction literature and film to consider which scientific and social issues the works address, how accurate or plausible the predictions are, and evaluate these works for our own use. Authors will include Philip K. Dick, William Gibson, Neal Stephenson, Kim Stanley Robinson and Iain Banks.

You will also be able to view entire films of speculative fiction related to our topics in the parallel course English Through Cinema!
objective: After finishing this course you will be familiar with the most common tropes of SF and have thought critically about technological developments based on scenarios presented in works of SF.
prerequisites: This course requires a large amount of reading, speaking as well as listening and writing at the C1 level. Therefore it is recommended for students who scored at least 60 percent on the English placement test. Exceptions can be made in the case of exceptionally motivated students.
title: English - The Science of Science Fiction C1

name: English - Critical Thinking and Science Writing C2
English - Scientific Presentation and Writing C2
content:
Combining elements of our presentation and writing skills courses, this course covers a variety of communication techniques needed for a successful career in science.
In this course students write and revise texts of various types while learning how to evaluate and interpret written texts of others in regular workshop sessions. Topics considered include: comparison and contrast, data commentary, as well as writing summaries and critiques. In the oral presentation part of the course, this course allows students to practice for formal speaking tasks in English such as a class presentation, dissertation defense or conference talk.
objective:
After completion of this module, students have improved their ability to communicate clearly and powerfully in formal written English, become familiar with some common forms of expository writing, increased academic, professional and everyday vocabulary, developed regular habits to continue this learning process, and generally have increased their enjoyment of writing.

In addition, students can understand formal texts with increased ease, summarize information from different written sources, reconstructing arguments and accounts in a coherent presentation; they can express themselves spontaneously very fluently and precisely, differentiating finer shades of meaning even in more complex situations.
prerequisites: This is a C2 level course and you need to complete the placement test before the first lesson (bring a printout if your result!).
title: English - Scientific Presentation and Writing C2

name: English - English for Political Science C1
content:
This course prepares students to read and understand political science texts in English. The texts have been chosen by various professors at the HfP, covering the fields of political theory, comparative politics, and international relations. We will especially focus on interpreting these texts in light of current affairs. 

Class time will be largely dedicated to discussions, presentations, and text analysis. The course emphasizes expanding vocabulary, spoken fluency, and persuasive writing and argumentation skills.

Graded tasks include an oral presentation (20%), multiple drafts of an essay (1000-1200 words, 40%), online forum posts (10%), and a final written examination (30%).

Frequently Asked Questions:
  -  "Is this course an easy way to get 3 ECTS points with no work?" - No.
  -  "Will I improve my English a ton and enjoy myself in the process?" - Yes.
objective: After completing this course, students will be able to more fluently read and discuss political science academic texts in English. They will have expanded their active vocabulary.
prerequisites: Ability to work at the C1 level, as demonstrated through the placement test in Moodle
title: English - English for Political Science C1

name: English - Literature, Technology and Society C1
content:
Advances in science and technology have gone hand-in-hand with social change starting with the earliest human advances in the stone and metal ages, through the industrial revolution, all the way to the digital age and beyond. 

In this seminar, five instructors have chosen works of literature to spark discussions about the interaction between technology and society. We're looking forward to this chance to hear your ideas and share ours.

SPOILER ALERT! You should plan to read the book before the class - or at least have made a very good start. If you have trouble locating any of the books, please get in touch with Rose Jacobs (rose.jacobs@tum.de) as we will make some available for students to borrow.
objective: Understanding of and ability to analyse complex literary texts and think critically about the role of technolgy in society.
prerequisites: You should have a C1-level result or higher on the placement test.
title: English - Literature, Technology and Society C1

name: English - English for Automotive Engineers C1
content:
This module focuses on English-language communication and technical vocabulary in the automotive industry. Classes are arranged thematically around automotive topics of interest, such as the engine, electric cars, driverless cars, etc.

The module includes opportunities for students to practice both written and oral communication needed in professional life, with emphasis on soft skill areas such as meetings, information acquisition, presentations, team collaboration, and reports, as well as aspects of intercultural communication needed for achieving professional success.
objective: After completion of this module, students will be prepared to communicate professionally in English. They will be able to read, write, and speak about a range of technical topics with greater fluency and accuracy. The students will be required to express themselves in both written and spoken contexts, and to show improvement in their use of the language.
prerequisites: Ability to begin work at the C1 level as evidenced by the placement test at www.moodle.tum.de.
title: English - English for Automotive Engineers C1

name: English - Intensive Thesis Writers' Workshop C2
content: This course is designed for students currently writing theses or dissertations in English. It combines lectures and workshopping texts in small groups. The content goes beyond mere questions of “correct” grammar and word choice, and emphasizes instead stylistic guidelines for forceful and clear English writing on a high academic level. Discussions have a slight emphasis on strategies for German speakers but are still appropriate for students from any language background. Students are encouraged to make use of the English Writing Center during or after this course to receive additional one-to-one support.
title: English - Intensive Thesis Writers' Workshop C2

name: English - Controversial Topics in Science and Technology C1
content:
In this hybrid course, students will improve their English by studying and discussing controversial issues in science and technology. The students themselves will determine the specific topics, which they will research and present individually or in small groups.  

Past student topics include the following:

- gene editing in children
- LLMs in university learning
- the nature of consciousness
- climate change debates
- how to label GMO foods
- the future of energy
- biodiversity
- animal ethics
-living architecture

Class time will be largely dedicated to presentations, discussions, and debates. The course emphasizes building vocabulary and spoken fluency but will also help students improve their writing skills.

In-person attendance is best when possible; however, students may attend online as needed.
objective: develop your spoken fluency in English
prerequisites: C1 level of English, verified through the English Placement Test (in Moodle)
title: English - Controversial Topics in Science and Technology C1

name: English - Gateway to English Master's C1
categories: Social and Political Aspects of Data Science
content: This course enables students to communicate competently about geodesy in English, thus preparing them for postgraduate study in their field. Students will learn how to deliver effective academic writing and presentations in English, how to handle exam questions in English and will have ample opportunity to develop speaking skills and communicative competence around geodetic issues which interest them.
objective:
Students will be competent in the level of English required to study the Master’s in Geodesy and Geoinformation course. Students will feel comfortable reading, writing and talking about geodetic topics in English.

As part of the Gateway to English Master's module, successful completion of this course fulfills the English requirement for any master's degree course at TUM.
prerequisites: Ability to begin work at the C1 level (or just below) of the GER as evidenced by a score of at least 50 percent on the placement test at www.elearning.tum.de. (Please check current announcements as the exact percentages may vary each semester.)
title: English - Englisch - English for Geodesy: Gateway to English Master’s C1

name: English - English Pronunciation C1
content:
The course will review both segmental and non-segmental phonology (sounds and connected speech), covering areas such as vowel and consonant production, stress placement, and intonation in English.

Where appropriate, comparisons will be drawn between different languages as well as different varieties of English (e.g. U.S. varities and British English varieties).
objective: The course aims to provide you with an in-depth understanding of the main features and challenges involved in pronouncing English clearly. The course is not designed to promote any particular accent or variety, but rather to enable you to communicate more effectively in English with both native and non-native speakers in business, academic and everyday situations.
prerequisites: This course is intended for those students who have either already completed the course 'Introduction to English Pronunciation' or whose pronunciation is already at a more adavanced level, and who wish to extend their knowledge and pratice their pronunciation further.
title: English - English Pronunciation C1

name: English - English Conversation Partners Program B1-C1+
content:
An informal class in which lower/ intermediate-level (approximately B1 of the GER) English speakers are placed in small groups with upper-level (approximately C1+ of the GER) speakers to practice English conversation in a fun and friendly environment. The class will meet regularly throughout the semester for larger group activities, but the majority of speaking practice will be done within the small groups, on students' own schedules. 

Regardless of their level, all students are equal partners in the course: More confident speakers should be willing to take on a guiding role, and everyone should be culturally inquisitive, open-minded and keen to talk. We hope that alongside conversational practice and improvement you will find interesting cultural exchange and perhaps new friends in a mixed nationality class.  

This course is offered on a pass/fail basis and is worth 2 ECTS points. To pass the course, students are required to attend class meetings, to participate actively in their group activities (keeping a “conversation diary”), and to contribute to a group assignment (to be specified by the lecturer).
objective: With the opportunity to converse in English on a regular basis and on a broad range of topics, students will increase their confidence and proficiency in speaking. Through a mix of teacher-led and private meetings, students will become aware of available resources for improving their English skills autonomously.
prerequisites: English speaking skills at approximately the B1-C2 level of the GER. PLEASE COMPLETE THE PLACEMENT TEST BEFORE YOU REGISTER!
title: English - English Conversation Partners Program B1 - C1+

name: English - Creative Writing C1: Introduction to Narrative Strategies and Literary Forms
content:
Sparking your Creativity: Exploring Varied Narrative Forms as a Tool to Improve Academic Writing and Rhetorical Skills

The ‘Introduction to Narrative Forms and Strategies’ course provides students with a stimulating overview of a range of narrative forms, tools and rhetorical devices. Some of the forms covered include contemporary nature writing, games narrative design and hybrid narrative essays. In the course, students will have the opportunity to experiment with some of these forms and try out many of the storytelling instruments and concepts first-hand.

Critical reading assignments focusing on the interplay between language, form and content will aid students in exploring the rules and strategies of composition used in both fiction and non-fiction genres and enable them to engage more closely with the English language to develop linguistic dexterity therein. 

Current theories of literary and cultural criticism will be introduced and students will be expected to critically evaluate model texts as well as their own writing whilst being encouraged to appraise, support and critique the writing of their peers in a guided workshop environment. 

A component covering revision and structural editing techniques will help prepare students for both academic and non-fiction publishing. 

The performative aspects of the writing industry including public performances and speaking (readings and discussions) will be touched upon and other issues related to being a writer i.e. the road to publication and the ethics of writing will also be discussed.
objective: Enhanced rhetorical and composition skills. Practicing and analyzing a variety of narrative forms will aid STEM students to develop an aptitude for creative problem solving and help them learn how to tolerate uncertainty in process and outcome whilst embracing creative and intellectual risk as well as develop their critical vocabulary in feedback sessions.
prerequisites: No previous knowledge is required
title: English - Creative Writing C1: Introduction to Narrative Strategies and Literary Forms

name: English - Creative Writing C1: The Art of Craft - Toward Publication: Critical Revision Techniques
content:
In the Advanced Fiction Writing Course, students who are already familiar with the basics of narratology can further explore other fiction and non-fiction genres, the interplay between form and content and further deepen their writing abilities to achieve well-organized, rhetorically effective English prose. Students will also appraise, support and critique the literary writing of their peers in a guided workshop environment.

Revision techniques will be covered and more complex theories of literary criticism will be explored and applied to contemporary texts and their texts. Other issues related to being a writer i.e. the road to publication, the ethics of writing (cultural appropriation etc.) will also be discussed.

To this end, below are three additional components that will be included in the syllabus.

- A component on Manuscript Preparation for Publication and Revision Techniques; a transferable skill which will help prepare students for academic and non-fiction publishing too.

- A focus on the performative aspects of the writing industry including public performances and speaking (readings and discussions).
Please note that the public performances component is currently not possible due to the current Corona Virus regulations but class readings and discussions will still take place.

- An introduction to other new forms not yet covered in the introductory CW course- Forms eg. screenwriting, nature writing and / or travelogues.

Manuscript Preparation for Publication:

-	Editing – structural editing, proofreading etc.

How to write:
-	Book Blurbs
-	Reviews
-	Synopsis
-	A letter to the Editor

Editorial experience assisting in practicum with the T.U.M Sprachenzentrum English Department literary journal- Polyphony
prerequisites: Beginners and experienced creative writers are welcome.
title: English - Creative Writing C1: The Art of Craft - Toward Publication: Critical Revision Techniques

name: French A1.1
content: In this module, students gain basic knowledge of French as a foreign language, enabling them to successfully manage basic everyday situations with minimal language skills, e.g introducing themselves and others; talking about free-time activities; asking for information and for directions; shopping. Grammar topics include: present tense of regular and irregular verbs; personal pronouns; definite, indefinite and partitive articles; questions; and adjective declension. Moreover, opportunities will be made available for students to more effectively organize the process of learning French as a foreign language and thus to improve their own learning abilities.
objective: The module is aimed at level A1 "Elementary Language Use" of the CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference). Students gain basic knowledge of French as a foreign language with a general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural and cultural aspects. After completion of this module, students will be able to ask and answer questions about familiar topics. They can interact in a simple fashion, provided that their counterpart speaks slowly and clearly and is willing to help; they can briefly describe themselves in writing.
prerequisites: None
title: French A 1.1

name: French A1.2
content: In this module, students expand their basic knowledge of French lexis and grammar for simple oral and written for every-day communication situations. They learn, for example, to pose questions to others about themselves and their families and to answer similar questions, to make arrangements as well as reservations in hotels, to report on free time and holiday activities, to describe past events and habits. Grammar covered will include: Passé Composé, Futur proche, quantities, possessive pronouns, direct and indirect object pronouns. Strategies will be taught enabling students with minimal language skills to successfully manage basic everyday situations. Moreover, opportunities will be made available to more effectively organize the learning process of French as a foreign language and to improve the ability to learn.
objective: The module is aimed at level A1 "Elementary Language Use" of the CEFR. Students gain basic knowledge of French as a foreign language with a general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural and cultural aspects. After completion of this module, students will be able to use and understand everyday expressions and very simple sentences. They can interact in a simple fashion, provided that their counterpart speaks slowly and clearly and is willing to help; they can write short, simple reports in French using fixed phrases.
prerequisites: Sound knowledge of level A1.1; placement test result A1.2.
title: French A 1.2

name: French A2.1
content: In this module, students gain additional basic knowledge of French as a foreign language, enabling them to successfully manage everyday situations, e.g. while travelling, at the doctor, while looking for a place to live, or while talking to colleagues, friends and neighbors. More grammar will be covered, e.g. use of the Passé Composé und Imparfait, the conditional, relative pronouns, en + y pronouns, comparatives and the superlative. Students will learn strategies for successfully communicating in day-to-day situations with minimal language skills. Additionally, opportunities will be made available to more effectively learn French as a foreign language and thus to improve the student's ability to learn.
objective: The module is aimed at level "A2 - Elementary Language Use" of the CEFR. Students gain basic knowledge of French as a foreign language with general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural and cultural aspects. After completion of this module, students will be able to understand and use simple sentences and expressions on a broader spectrum of familiar topics. Students can, for example, describe where they live, their health status and free-time activities. They are able to communicate while searching for a place to live and in important situations while on holiday or travelling and describe the resulting experiences or events. They can use and understand standard expressions in familiar communication situations both orally and in writing.
prerequisites: Sound knowledge of level A1; placement test results A2.1
title: French A 2.1

name: French A2.2
content: In this module, students gain further basic knowledge of French as a foreign language, enabling them to successfully deal with every-day situations. Listening and reading comprehension as well as speaking will be practiced with various listening exercises and texts (the world of work, new media, environmental protection, culture). The review and extension of grammar refers to communicative learning goals (emphasis: the future, gerunds, indirect speech, past perfect, the subjunctive). Students will learn strategies for successfully communicating orally and in writing with minimal language skills. Additionally, opportunities will be made available to more effectively learn French as a foreign language and thus to improve the student's ability to learn.
objective: This module is aimed at level "A2 Basic Language Use" of the CEFR. Students gain further basic knowledge of French as a foreign language with general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural and cultural aspects. After completion of this module, in discussions students will be able to understand and use familiar sentences and figures of speech on an expanded spectrum of topics, such as basic information on every-day topics or topics relating to the university and careers. They can understand longer texts and letters on familiar topics in which contemporary but simple every-day and business language is used and in which expected information is found. Students are able to write short, informative texts or reports on every-day situations and the university.
prerequisites: Sound knowledge of Level A2.1; placement test results A2.2.
title: French A 2.2

name: French B1.1
content: In this module, knowledge of French as a foreign language will be further developed, enabling students to function/persuade/express themselves in French independently and confidently in familiar situations, e.g. in the classroom, at work, in free time and with the family, on topics of general interest when standard French is spoken. Students expand their cultural knowledge of a great variety of current topics in French life. They increase their vocabulary as well as consolidate and deepen the French grammar focused on thus far.
objective: The module is aimed at level "B1 Independent Language use" of the CEFR. Students acquire knowledge of French as a foreign language at the standard language level with a focus on intercultural, cultural and academic aspects. Following completion of this module, students can communicate confidently in familiar situations encountered at school or work, in free-time activities or while travelling in French-speaking countries. They can understand the essential content of simple, authentic texts on every-day topics and can take part in discussions on familiar topics. Students are capable of describing personal experiences and impressions in writing in longer texts.
prerequisites: Sound knowledge of Level A2; placement test result B1.1.
title: French B1.1

name: French B1.2
content: In this module, knowledge of French as a foreign language will be further developed, enabling students to express themselves in French independently and confidently in familiar situations, e.g. in the classroom, at work, in free time and with the family, on topics of general interest, e.g. films, music, sports, etc, when standard French is spoken. Students expand their cultural knowledge of a great variety of current topics in French life. They increase their vocabulary as well as consolidate and deepen the French grammar focused on thus far.
objective: The module is aimed at level B1 of the CEFR. Students acquire knowledge of French as a foreign language at the standard language level with a focus on intercultural, cultural and academic aspects. Following completion of this module, students can confidently communicate in most situations they are likely to encounter in school, at work, during free-time or while travelling in French-speaking countries. They can understand and describe the essential content of simple specialist texts, radio or television programs, and literary texts and spontaneously take part in discussions of familiar topics of general interest. They can write simple, formal and longer personal letters and texts, report in a structured fashion on a general topic of personal interest and take a logical position on a current topic, if support is offered.
prerequisites: Sound knowledge of B1.1; placement test result B1.2
title: French Language Intermediate B1.2

name: French B2 - French for the profession
content: In this module, students will increase their knowledge of French as a foreign language, enabling them to discuss with a native speaker topics of general or professional interest actively and with a certain degree of fluency and to argue for a position in a comprehensible fashion. On the one hand, the module provides an introducation to the French business world and, on the other hand, prepares students to study in a French-speaking region. Particular attention will be devoted to the development of communication skills and intercultural competencies. Certain grammatical structures will be reviewed and studied in greater depth to consolidate oral and writing skills. In this module, applying for jobs in France is a central focus.
objective: The module is aimed at level "B2 Independent Language Use" of the CEFR. Students acquire knowledge of French as a foreign language at the standard language level with a focus on intercultural, cultural and academic aspects. Following completion of this module, with their intercultural knowledge, students can communicate appropriately about the university and the business world in French-speaking regions and seek a professional training program or further education in those regions.
prerequisites: Sound knowledge of level B.1; placement test result B.2
title: French B2 Le francais pour la profession

name: French B2/C1 - France currently
content: In this module, knowledge of French as a foreign language will be further developed, enabling students to communicate with a native speaker actively and with a certain degree of fluency on topics of general interest or in familiar specialist areas and to argue a point understandably. In order to consolidate speaking and writing skills, certain French grammatical structures will be reviewed and extended. This module offers a cross-section of contemporary French culture, in which social tendencies, as reflected in newspaper articles, and radio and television programs, will be discussed. Topics suggested by students for examination are welcome. Students must independently prepare and deliver a short presentation on a cultural, social or scientific topic connected with France and then answer questions afterward.
objective: The module is aimed at level B2-C1 of the CEFR, depending on the level of the student's knowledge. Students acquire knowledge of French as a foreign language at the standard language level with a focus on intercultural, cultural and academic aspects. Following completion of this module, students can report on texts in detail and coherently, summarize information, describe their impressions, and defend their positions. They can describe the content of texts, discussions, or television programs and offer their opinions. They are capable of spontaneously and fluently expressing themselves, without obviously having to search for words. Students can communicate clearly and in a structured fashion, both orally and in writing, on many topics in their areas of interest or specialization.
prerequisites: Sound knowledge of Level B.1; placement test result B.2.
title: French B2/C1 La France actuelle

name: French B1/B2 - Conversation Course: French Society
content:
In dieser LV werden Kenntnisse in der Fremdsprache Französisch erarbeitet, die es den Studierenden ermöglichen, (sich) in verschiedenen Situationen, z.B.  in Studium, Arbeit und Freizeit, und zu Themen von allgemeinem Interesse selbständig und sicher in der Zielsprache zu operieren/bewegen/verständigen. Dabei werden interkulturelle, landeskundliche und studienbezogene Aspekte berücksichtigt. Je nach Bedarf werden Schwerpunkte der französischen Grammatik wiederholt und vertieft.
Presseartikel, Nachrichten aus dem Internet, etc. bieten einen Querschnitt durch die gegenwärtige französische Gesellschaft an und bilden somit die Grundlage für die mündliche Kommunikation. Die aktive Mitarbeit der Studierenden z. B. mittels Kurzvorträgen, Diskussionen wird erwartet und gefördert. Ziel dieser LV ist außerdem, die Studierenden auf einen Studienaufenthalt im frankophonen Sprachraum (Kanada, ERASMUS, etc.) vorzubereiten.
objective: Die LV orientiert sich am Niveau B 1 - B 2 des GER. Nach der Teilnahme an der Modulveranstaltung können die Studierenden, je nach Wissenstand, über verschiedene Themen detaillierte, zusammenhängende Texte berichten, Informationen zusammenfassen, ihre Erfahrungen und Eindrücke wiedergeben, ihren Standpunkt vertreten. Sie können Inhalte von Lektüren, Gespräche oder Sendungen wiedergeben und ihre Meinung vertreten.Nach Abschluss des Moduls sind sie in der Lage, zu vielen Themen aus ihren Interessen- oder Fachgebieten klar und strukturiert in mündlicher und schriftlicher Form zu kommunizieren.
prerequisites: Erfolgreiche Teilnahme an der Stufe B1.1 oder vergleichbare Kenntnisse; Einstufungstest mit dem Ergebnis B 1
title: French B1/B2 Conversation Course: French Society

name: French B2 - Communication Course
content:
In diesem Modul werden Kenntnisse in der Fremdsprache Französisch aufgebaut und vertieft, die es den Studierenden ermöglichen, aktiv und mit einem gewissen Grad an Flüssigkeit über Themen von allgemeinem Interesse oder von vertrautem Fachgebiet mit einem Muttersprachler zu diskutieren und eine Argumentation gut verständlich ausführen.
Ein besonderes Merkmal wird in diesem Modul auf die Entwicklung von Lesestrategien von allgemeinen und fachbezogenen Texten, auf Wortschatzarbeit und die Entwicklung von Hörstrategien gelegt. Zur Festigung der mündlichen und schriftlichen Fertigkeit werden Schwerpunkte der Grammatik wiederholt und vertieft.
objective:
Das Modul orientiert sich am Niveau „B2- Selbständige Sprachverwendung“ des GER. Der/die Studierende kann den wesentlichen Inhalt von Artikeln und Berichten sowie Texte aus dem eigenen Fach- und Interessengebiet selbständig verstehen. 
Er/sie kann längere Redebeiträge und Vorträge zu aktuellen Themen folgen, sofern sie klar vorgetragen werden. 
Er/sie ist in der Lage Texte zu aktuellen Themen zu schreiben und dabei auch zu einem gewissen Grad komplexe Satzstrukturen zu benutzen. 
Er/sie kann zu vielen Themen aus seinen/ihren Interessen- oder Fachgebieten klar in mündlicher Form kommunizieren.
prerequisites:
- gesicherte Kenntnisse der Stufe B1
- Einstufungstest mit Ergebnis B2
title: French B2 - Conversation Course

name: French C1 - Upper Conversation Course
content: In this module, students will increase their knowledge of French as a foreign language, enabling them, both orally and in writing, to deal appropriately (act and react) with topics from day-to-day life, work and the culture of French-speaking regions. Using texts, current news articles, and excerpts from radio and televison programs, they will engage with the socio-cultural context of current issues. Topics suggested by students for examination are welcome. Knowledge in these areas will be increased and elements of grammar will be reviewed and fine-tuned. Students must independently prepare and deliver a short presentation on a cultural, social or scientific topic connected with France and then answer questions afterward.
objective: The module is aimed at level "C1 Proficient language use" of the CEFR. Students acquire knowledge of French as a foreign language with a focus on intercultural, cultural and academic aspects. Following completion of this course, students can communicate at a very high level, both orally and in writing, in a wide variety of situations. They are capable of effectively and flexibly using the foreign language in study abroad as well as on the job. They can understand a broad spectrum of longer, more challenging texts and recognize the implicit arguments. They can speak spontaneously and fluently, without having to frequently and obviously search for words. They can produce clear, structured and detailed texts on complex topics and in so doing appropriately employ organizational devices and connectors.
prerequisites: Sound knowledge of level B2; placement test result C1
title: French - advanced level C1 - Cours de conversation supérieure

name: French B2 - Preparation Course for University Exchange
content:
Die LV bereitet auf ein ausländisches Studium oder Praktikum in einem frankophonen Land vor, indem es verschiedene Aspekte der Kultur und der Gesellschaft aufgreift. und somit die interkulturelle Kompetenz und Performanz erhöht werden.
Im Vordergrund stehen folgende Komponenten:
-	Sprachliche und praktische Vorbereitung auf einen Studienaufenthalt an einer frankophonen Universität 
-	Vermittlung von Umgangsstrategien mit fremden Strukturen und Formen (Hochschullandschaft, Lehr-und Lernformen, Kommunikationsformen)
-	Schärfung des Bewusstseins für interkulturelle Aspekte
-	Bewerbung
-	Entwicklung von Hörstrategien
-	Einführung in die Praxis schriftlicher akademischer Arbeit
Zur Festigung der mündlichen und schriftlichen Fertigkeit werden Schwerpunkte der Grammatik wiederholt und vertieft.
objective: Die LV orientiert sich am Niveau „B2- Selbständige Sprachverwendung“ des GER. Der/die Studierende ist in der Lage, durch situationsrelevantes interkulturelles Wissen über Universitäten und Berufswelt im französischen Sprachraum angemessen zu kommunizieren und einen Studien-, Projekt- oder Forschungsaufenthalt, ein Praktikum oder Weiterbildungsmaßnahmen im französischen Sprachraum zu absolvieren.
prerequisites:
- gesicherte Kenntnisse der Stufe B 1
- Einstufungstest mit Ergebnis B 2
title: French - B2 - Preparation Course for a semester abroad

name: French B2 Technical French
content:
Das Modul führt einerseits in die französische Fachsprache im technischen Bereich und andererseits bereitet auf ein ausländisches Studium im einem frankophonen Land vor, indem es verschiedene Aspekte der Kultur und der Gesellschaft aufgreift, und somit die interkulturelle Kompetenz und Performanz erhöht werden.
Im Vordergrund stehen folgende Komponenten:
- Vermittlung einer Fachterminologie zu einzelnen studienrelevanten fachbezogenen Schwerpunkten
- Übung und Anwendung des Gelernten in relevanten interaktiven  Kontexten
- Schärfung des Bewusstseins für interkulturelle Aspekte
- Erweiterung der Handlungsfähigkeit in der Fremdsprache auf komplexe Sprechsituationen mit fachsprachlichem Inhalt
- Entwicklung von Lesekompetenz von wissenschafts- u. fachbezogenen Texten
- Entwicklung von Hörstrategien
-Einführung in die Praxis schriftlich akademischer Arbeit
Zur Festigung der mündlichen und schriftlichen Fertigkeit werden Schwerpunkte der Grammatik wiederholt und vertieft.
objective: Das Modul orientiert sich am Niveau „B2- Selbständige Sprachverwendung“ des GER. Der/die Studierende kann den wesentlichen Inhalt von Artikeln und Berichten sowie Texte aus dem eigenen Fach- und Interessengebiet mühelos verstehen. Er/sie kann längere Redebeiträge und Vorträge sowohl zu aktuellen Themen als auch innerhalb seines/ihres Fachgebietes folgen, sofern sie klar vorgetragen werden. Er/sie ist in der Lage Texte im Kontext seines /ihres Studienfaches zu schreiben und dabei auch zu einem gewissen Grad komplexe Satzstrukturen und fachspezifisches Vokabular zu benutzen. Er/sie kann zu vielen Themen aus seinen/ihren Interessen- oder Fachgebieten klar und strukturiert in mündlicher Form kommunizieren. Er/Sie ist in der Lage, die Fremdsprache sowohl im Auslandsstudium als auch im Beruf wirksam und flexibel zu gebrauchen.
prerequisites:
- gesicherte Kenntnisse der Stufe B 1
- Einstufungstest mit Ergebnis B 2
title: French B 2 Technical French

name: French A1.1 + A1.2
content:
In dieser LV werden Grundkenntnisse in der Fremdsprache Französisch vermittelt, die es den Studierenden ermöglichen, sich in alltäglichen Grundsituationen trotz noch geringer Sprachkenntnisse zurechtzufinden. Dabei werden interkulturelle und landeskundliche Aspekte berücksichtigt. 
Der/Die Studierende lernt z.B., einfache Fragen zu Person und Familie zu stellen und zu beantworten sowie über Themen wie Studium, Beruf, Freizeit, Essen in einfachen Sätzen im Präsenz und Perfekt zu berichten. Es werden u.a. folgende grammatische Themen behandelt: Präsenz, Passé Composé, Futur proche, Artikel, Possessivbegleiter, direkte und indirekte Objektpronomen, Präpositionen, Fragesätze. Es werden Strategien vermittelt, die eine Verständigung trotz noch geringer Sprachkenntnisse in alltäglichen Grundsituationen ermöglichen. 
Außerdem werden Möglichkeiten aufgezeigt, den Lernprozess in der Fremdsprache Französisch effektiver zu gestalten und die eigene Lernfähigkeit zu verbessern.
objective:
Die LV orientiert sich am Niveau „A1 – Elementare Sprachverwendung“ des GER. Der/die Studierende erlangt nach der Teilnahme an der Modulveranstaltung Grundkenntnisse in der Fremdsprache Französisch mit allgemeiner Orientierung unter Berücksichtigung interkultureller und landeskundlicher Aspekte. Er/sie ist in der Lage, einfache Fragen über vertraute Themen zu stellen und zu beantworten. Er/sie kann sich auf einfache Art verständigen, wenn die Gesprächspartnerinnen oder Gesprächspartner langsam und deutlich sprechen und bereit sind zu helfen. Er/sie kann einfache schriftliche Mitteilungen zur Person machen.
Sowohl im mündlichen als auch im schriftlichen Sprachgebrauch ist der/die Studierende in der Lage, situationsadäquat, bzw. der A 1-Stufe entsprechend, Wortschatz und Grammatik korrekt anzuwenden.
prerequisites: keine
title: French A1.1 + A1.2 intensive

name: French C1 - French in Business
content:
In dieser LV werden Kenntnisse in der Fremdsprache Französisch aufgebaut und vertieft, die es den Studierenden ermöglichen, spontan und fließend über Themen von politischen, wirtschaftlichen oder gesellschaftlichen Interesse mit einem Muttersprachler zu diskutieren und eine Meinung strukturiert und überzeugend zu vertreten, ohne öfter deutlich erkennbar nach Worten suchen zu müssen. 
Die LV gibt einerseits eine Einleitung in das Französisch des Wirtschaftslebens und bereitet andererseits die Studierenden auf einen (Studien-)Aufenthalt im frankophonen Sprachraum vor. Besonderes Augenmerk wird auf die Entwicklung kommunikativer Fähigkeiten und interkultureller Kompetenz gelegt. Zur Festigung der mündlichen und schriftlichen Fertigkeit werden bei Bedarf Schwerpunkte der Grammatik wiederholt und vertieft. 
In dieser LV bilden ausgewählte volkswirtschaftliche Themen (Konsum, Rolle des Staates, diverse betriebliche Funktionen, Globalisierung, Nachhaltigkeit u. a.) eine zentrale Rolle.
objective: Die LV orientiert sich am Niveau C 1 Fachkundige Sprachkenntnisse des GER. Der/die Studierende ist in der Lage, durch relevantes interkulturelles Wissen über Berufs- und Wirtschaftswelt im französischen Sprachraum angemessen zu kommunizieren und einen Studienaufenthalt, ein Praktikum oder Weiterbildungsmaßnahmen im französischen Sprachraum anzustreben.
prerequisites:
- gesicherte Kenntnisse der Stufe B2
- Einstufungstest mit Ergebnis C1
- Vorkenntnisse in BWL und/oder VWL sind keineswegs erforderlich
title: French C1 - French in Business: Economics and Politics

name: French A2.1 + A2.2
content:
In dieser Lehrveranstaltung werden Grundkenntnisse in der Fremdsprache Französisch intensiv aufgebaut, die den Studierenden – trotz noch geringer Sprachkenntnisse - ermöglichen, sich in Alltagssituationen zurechtzufinden. Die Studierenden lernen/üben (u. a), wie man über Erfahrungen spricht und sie bewertet, wie man Meinungen äußert und darauf reagiert, wie man über die Ursachen und Folgen von etwas spricht, wie man Anweisungen, und Ratschläge gibt. Dabei werden interkulturelle und landeskundliche Aspekte berücksichtigt. Die grammatischen Strukturen werden weiter aufgebaut. Folgende grammatischen Themen werden behandelt, wie z.B. Verwendung von Passé Composé und Imparfait, Konditional, Relativpronomen, „en + y“ Pronomen, Komparativ und Superlativ.
Es werden Strategien vermittelt, die mündlich wie schriftlich eine Verständigung trotz noch geringer Sprachkenntnisse ermöglichen. Außerdem werden Möglichkeiten aufgezeigt, den Lernprozess effektiver zu gestalten und damit die eigene Lernfähigkeit zu verbessern. Ferner werden Möglichkeiten aufgezeigt, den Lernprozess in der Fremdsprache Französisch effektiver zu gestalten und damit die eigene Lernfähigkeit zu verbessern.
objective: Die LV orientiert sich am „A2 – Elementare Sprachverwendung“ des GER. Nach Abschluss dieser LV kann der/die Studierende einfache Sätze und Redewendungen zu einem erweiterten Spektrums an vertrauten Themen verstehen und gebrauchen. Dabei handelt es sich um grundlegende Informationen zu alltäglichen oder studien- bzw. berufsrelevanten Themen. Sie erfassen die Bedeutung von kurzen, klaren und deutlich artikulierten Mitteilungen und Durchsagen. Der/die Studierende kann standardsprachliche Ausdrücke in vertrauten Kommunikationssituationen sowohl in mündlicher als auch in schriftlicher Form verstehen und verwenden und dabei Wortschatz und Grammatik korrekt anzuwenden.
prerequisites:
- gesicherte Kenntnisse der Stufe A1
- Einstufungstest mit Ergebnis A2.1
title: French A2.1+A2.2

name: French C1 - oral and written expression
content:
In dieser LV werden Kenntnisse in der Fremdsprache Französisch erarbeitet, die es den Studierenden ermöglichen, schriftlich wie mündlich in Themenbereichen aus Alltag, Beruf und Kultur situationsadäquat zu handeln (agieren und reagieren). 
Die Studierenden überprüfen und vertiefen anhand komplex aufgebauter und anspruchsvoll formulierter Hör- und Lesetexte zu Themen von gesamtgesellschaftlichem Interesse ihre Fähigkeiten, ohne große Mühe und überwiegend flüssig in der Fremdsprache zu agieren.
Sie lernen, Textsorten und Schreibstile zu unterscheiden und situationsadäquat anzuwenden. Sie üben, komplexe Sachtexte auch außerhalb des eigenen Fachgebietes zu analysieren, zu komprimieren und kritisch schriftlich sowie mündlich zu kommentieren.
objective: Diese LV orientiert sich an Niveau "C1-Kompetente Sprachverwendung" des GER. Nach der Teilnahme an der Lehrveranstaltung kann der/die Studierende auf sehr hohem Niveau in unterschiedlichsten Situationen schriftlich und mündlich kommunizieren. Er/Sie ist in der Lage, die Fremdsprache mündlich und schriftlich sowohl im Auslandsstudium als auch im Beruf wirksam und flexibel zu gebrauchen. Er/Sie kann ein breites Spektrum anspruchsvoller, längerer Texte verstehen und auch implizite Bedeutungen erfassen. Er/Sie kann sich spontan und fließend ausdrücken, ohne öfter deutlich erkennbar nach Worten suchen zu müssen. Er/Sie kann sich klar, strukturiert und ausführlich zu komplexen Sachverhalten äußern und dabei verschiedene Mittel zur Textverknüpfung angemessen verwenden.
prerequisites:
- gesicherte Kenntnisse der Stufe B2
- Einstufungstest mit Ergebnis C1
title: French C1 - oral and written expression

name: Italian A1.1 + A1.2 - Intensive
content: In this course, students gain basic knowledge of Italian as a foreign language, enabling them with minimal language skills to successfully manage basic everyday situations, for example in a restaurant, in public transportation, during introductions, etc. Additionally, opportunities will be made available to effectively organize the process of learning Italian as a foreign language. Students learn/practice "communicative functions": to pose questions to others about themselves and their families and to answer similar questions; to understand and use numbers and prices and to tell time; fundamental vocabulary concerning studying, careers, hobbies, food and eating habits; and talking about their day-to-day activities in the present and past tenses using simple sentences. Grammar: nouns (Genus and Numerus), articles, adjectives and declinations; indicative present of regular and irregular verbs; modal verbs; indicative perfect (only regular participles); question pronouns; simple and double negatives; prepositions without articles and compound prepositions; prepositions for the verbs essere/andare; object pronouns with and without emphasis; demonstrative pronouns questo/quello; indefinite pronouns molto, tanto, parecchio, poco; possessive pronouns; gerund (stare + gerundio); reflexive verbs; adverbs of time; basic numbers. Phonetics and orthography: alphabet; sound and writing; accent and pronunciation; intonation: statements, questions and exclamations.
objective: This course is aimed at level A1 of the CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference). Students gain basic knowledge of Italian as a foreign language with a general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural and cultural aspects. After completion of this module, students will be able to use and understand everyday expressions and very simple sentences (orally and in writing). They can introduce themselves and others, ask others about themselves and answer similar questions, give simple descriptions of their day-to-day lives and briefly describe themselves in writing. Students will be able to talk about their likes and dislikes, arrange to meet someone and communicate their wants/needs, for example, while shopping or in a restaurant.
prerequisites: None
title: Italian A 1.1 and A 1.2 - Intensive

name: Italian A1.1
content: In this course, students gain basic knowledge of Italian as a foreign language, enabling them with minimal language skills to successfully manage basic everyday situations, for example in a restaurant, in public transportation, during introductions, etc. Additionally, opportunities will be made available to effectively organize the process of learning Italian as a foreign language. Students learn/practice "communicative functions": to pose questions to others about themselves and their families and to answer similar questions; to understand and use numbers and prices; fundamental vocabulary concerning studying, careers, an average day, food and eating habits; and talking about their day-to-day activities in the present tense using simple sentences. Grammar: nouns (Genus and Numerus), articles, adjectives and declinations; indicative present of regular and irregular verbs; modal verbs; question pronouns; simple and double negatives; prepositions without articles; adverbs of time; basic numbers. Phonetics and orthography: alphabet; sound and writing; accent and pronunciation; intonation: statements, questions and exclamations.
objective: This course is aimed at level A1 of the CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference). Students gain basic knowledge of Italian as a foreign language with a general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural and cultural aspects. After completion of this module, students will be able to use and understand everyday expressions and very simple sentences (orally and in writing). They can introduce themselves and others, ask others about themselves and answer similar questions, give simple descriptions of their day-to-day lives and briefly describe themselves in writing.
prerequisites: None
title: Italian A 1.1

name: Italian C1 - Italian Communication: Language and Conversation
content:
Using specialized exercises, the students gain a knowledge to communicate actively. Main focus is laid upon cultural aspects and recent events reflected in literature, articles or movies.
In order to improve spoken skills, sentence structure is revised and improved and the vocabulary is increased.
objective: The module is aimed at level B2-C1 of the CEFR, depending on the level of the student's knowledge. Students acquire knowledge of Italian as a foreign language at the standard language level with a focus on intercultural, cultural and academic aspects. Following completion of this module, students can report on texts in detail and coherently, summarize information, describe their impressions, and defend their positions. They can describe the content of texts, discussions, or television programs and offer their opinions. They are capable of spontaneously and fluently expressing themselves, without obviously having to search for words. Students can communicate clearly and in a structured fashion, both orally and in writing, on many topics in their areas of interest or specialization.
prerequisites:
Sound knowledge of Italian B1.2 or
placement test B2.1
title: Italian B2 - Comunicare in italiano: lingua e conversazione

name: Italian A1.2
content: In this course, students gain basic knowledge of Italian as a foreign language, enabling them to successfully manage basic everyday situations, for example, at the bank, in administrative offices, in stores, etc. Additionally, opportunities will be made available to effectively organize the process of learning Italian as a foreign language. Students learn/practice "communicative functions": to ask for and give directions; ask the date and time; to express their opinions; to describe a place; to talk about their day-to-day activities in the present and perfect tenses using simple sentences. They learn basic vocabulary concerning daily life, job and hobbies. Grammar: compound prepositions; prepositions used with the verbs essere/andare; stressed and unstressed object pronouns; demonstrative pronouns questo/quello; indefinite pronouns molto, tanto, parecchio, poco; possessive pronouns; gerund (stare + gerundio); reflexive verbs; indicative perfect (only regular participles); ordinal numbers.
objective: This course refers to level A1 of the CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference). Students gain basic knowledge of Italian as a foreign language with a general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural and cultural aspects. After completion of this module, students will be able to use and understand everyday expressions and very simple sentences (orally and in writing). They can talk, among other things, about their likes and dislikes, arrange to meet someone and effectively communicate their wants/needs, for example, while shopping or looking for accommodations.
prerequisites: Passing grade at A1.1
title: Italian A 1.2

name: Italian A2.1
content: In this course, students gain basic knowledge of Italian as a foreign language, enabling them with minimal language skills to successfully manage basic everyday situations in both written and oral communication. Additionally, opportunities will be made available to effectively organize the process of learning Italian as a foreign language. Students learn/practice "communicative functions": to report in past tense (simple past) about their experiences; to talk about situations, people, and everyday activities in the past tense (simple past/present perfect); to provide descriptions of people (physical description and character traits); make comparisons between two things. Grammar: Passato prossimo regular and irregular verbs; Passato prossimo modal and reflexive verbs; Imperfetto; the use of Passato prossimo and Imperfetto; the conjunctions mentre and quando; possessive pronouns with relational terms (family, relatives); comparative and superlative.
objective: This course refers to level A2 of the CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference). Students gain basic knowledge of Italian as a foreign language with a general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural and cultural aspects. After completion of this course, students will be able to understand relevant spoken and written information on familiar topics and provide fairly detailed accounts of their experiences in past tense (perfect and imperfect).
prerequisites: Sound knowledge of module A1.2; placement test level A2.1.
title: Italian A 2.1

name: Italian A2.1 + A2.2 - Intensive
content: In this course, students gain basic knowledge of Italian as a foreign language, enabling them to successfully manage basic everyday situations. Student will learn strategies for communicating verbally and in writing despite limited language skills in the foreign language. Students learn/practice "communicative functions": to talk about personal experiences in past tense (simple past); to talk about situations/people and everyday activities in past tense (simple past and present perfect); to describe people; to make comparisons; to ask for advice, to give advice/directions to others; to express their wants/needs; to make hypotheses; to talk about future plans; to aks for and make suggestions; to ask for and provide information about past events; to give reasons for a decision; to use basic vocabulary on topics such as clothing and shopping habits, education and professional life. GRAMMAR: Passato prossimo regular and irregular verbs; Passato prossimo modal and reflexive verbs; Imperfetto; use of Passato prossimo and Imperfetto; conjuctions mentre and quando; Possessiva with relational terms (family/relatives); comparative and superlative; conditional; imperative; pronouns in combination with imperative; indicative future I; irregular plural constructions of Substantiva; relative pronouns chi, che, cui; Passato prossimo with object pronouns.
objective: This course refers to level A2 of the CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference). Students gain basic knowledge of Italian as a foreign language with a general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural and cultural aspects. After completion of this course, students will be able to understand relevant spoken and written information on familiar topics. They can express themselves verbally and in writing on familiar topics concerning family, studies, and hobbies using key grammatical structures and an adequate but still limited vocabulary.
prerequisites: Sound knowledge of module A1.2; placement test level A2.1.
title: Italian A 2.1 and A 2.2 - Intensive

name: Italian A2.2/B1.1 for Medicines
content: This seminar is designed for all medical students, in particular, those planning to participate in an exchange program (Erasmus, Praktikum, Famulatur etc.) It provides an introduction to medical terminology in Italian: 1. Fundamental human anatomy 2. anamnesis on the basis of selected case studies 3. doctor-patient consultation. Students gain insight into the health and medical systems in Italian-speaking regions. Selected basic language structures will be reviewed and supplemented to strengthen verbal and written skills; vocabulary expansion.
objective: Mastery of essential medical terminology.
prerequisites: Sound knowledge of module A2.1 or equivalent, placement test level A2.2 /B1.1
title: Italian for Medicine A2/B1

name: Italian B1.1
content: In this course, students expand their knowledge of Italian as a foreign language, enabling them to communicate independently and confidently in familiar situations at school, work, leisure, etc., when standard Italian is spoken. Students learn/practice "communicative functions": to talk about their tastes in music and literature; to write brief summaries of texts; to formulate opinions, to give reasons for and defend them; to express needs, hopes, doubts and fears. "Grammar": conjunctions; combined object pronouns; position of combined pronouns in Passato prossimo; emphasis of object pronouns; Trapassato prossimo; Passato remoto; Futuro II; temporal sequence in Passato prossimo and Trapassato prossimo and in sentences using Futuro I and Futuro II; irregular comparative and superlative forms; Indefinita ogni, ognuno, ciascuno, qualcuno, chiunque etc.; impersonal constructions; pronominal verbs accorgersene, cavarsela, andarsene, farcela etc.; word formation.
objective: This course refers to level B1 of the CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference).Students gain basic knowledge of Italian as a foreign language with a general language orientation while taking into consideration intercultural, cultural aspects, as well as issues related to their course of study. After completion of this course, students are able to communicate verbally and in writing about experiences and events using simple, connected grammatical structures, to describe their feelings and express opinions on familiar topics.
prerequisites: Sound knowledge of module A2.2; placement test level B1.1.
title: Italian B1.1

name: Italian B1.2
content: In this course, students expand their knowledge of Italian as a foreign language, enabling them to communicate independently and confidently in familiar situations at school, work, leisure, and the family about topics of general interest such as the environment, nature, immigration and society, when standard Italian is spoken. Students learn/practice "communicative functions": to compare opinions; express doubts, reservations, contrasting opinions; to give detailed descriptions of a place; make hypotheses; articulate requirements; communicate online. "Grammar": Futuro (I and II); impersonal constructions; Congiuntivo presente e passato; conjunctions with congiuntivo; congiuntivo in main clauses; prepositions of place and adverbs; placement of aggettivi qualificativi.
